messages:
maria: Heads up — running long-context loadtest on mixed cluster (2xA100 + 1xH100) and seeing KV cache memory steadily increase over ~2 hours until OOM on H100 node. Looks like page-table entries are not being reclaimed after evict, or a reuse index is getting duplicated. Repro steps below.

kai: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro + diff between a100/h100 traces?

maria: repro: run streaming chat with 24k token prompt, repeated 1800 s of concurrent 80 rps requests, model pinned to v1.3-quant. commands: 
```bash
./loadtest --model v1.3-quant --concurrency 80 --seq 24000 --duration 7200 --target-host cluster-1
```
Observations: A100 nodes peak then flatten; H100 node RSS keeps climbing by ~1.2GB per 10m. KV-cache allocations show new page allocations instead of reusing freed pages.

sanjay: can you dump the pagetable after a few evicts? what does the free-list look like?

maria: attached small dump snippet we collected from runtime page-table debug dump (sanitized):
```
# page_table dump @ 2026-03-16T10:22:13Z
pt[0x1a]=owner=GPU1,pg=0x7fdf00,flags=INUSE,gen=42
pt[0x1b]=owner=GPU1,pg=0x7fdf10,flags=FREE,gen=43
pt[0x1c]=owner=GPU1,pg=0x0,flags=RECLAIMED,gen=44
pt[0x1d]=owner=GPU1,pg=0x7fdf20,flags=INUSE,gen=42
# free_list: head=0x1b->0x2f->0x3a
# but allocator.stats shows free_pages=2
```
Problem: free_list contains 3 entries but allocator says 2 free pages. Also we see RECLAIMED entries with non-zero gen which later get reinserted.

aj: might be a race between eviction callback and async DMA when using a different kernel on H100. Kernel selection path selects fused-concurrent-copy for H100; that path defers the zeroing callback. if zero/free callback runs on different thread we might push the same page twice into freelist.

neha: interesting — we also see different batching distribution on H100 due to lower latency so the reuse-window heuristics behave differently (shorter reuse windows -> more frequent evict cycles). Could amplify a race.

maria: i added an extra sanity check in the runtime that prevents push if page->state != FREE and it stops the leak locally. patch:
```c
if (atomic_load(&page->state) != PAGE_FREE) {
  log("double-push prevented: idx=%u state=%u", idx, page->state);
  return;
}
push_free_list(page);
```
With that patch H100 memory stabilizes. But that's a bandaid; we need to root-cause whether it's kernel selection/dma ordering or page-table bookkeeping bug.

kai: can you capture the timeline around one evict + reuse where double-push occurs? i want to see call stacks and kernel types. ops-bot can we get perf traces for the H100 run?

ops-bot: perf trace job queued: perf-1898765432-h100-1 (will upload in ~10m) :robot_face:

sanjay: also check page->gen usage — if reuse increments gen and a late DMA completion references old gen, it could lead to stale mapping getting reused while still being counted. that would produce the seen RECLAIMED entries.

maria: i attached a small kernel-selection log excerpt where it picks kernels:
```
[kernel-select] model=v1.3-quant layer=attn type=kv-cache copy=concurrent-fused chosen=nvlink-copy-async
[kernel-select] model=v1.3-quant layer=ffn  chosen=matmul-epilogue
```
H100 run chooses nvlink-copy-async much more often than A100.

neha: suggestion: add a strict ordering barrier on eviction path before enqueueing page to free-list (i.e., wait for dma completion/fence) and measure perf impact. If stash shows leak stops, then it's ordering. If not, it's bookkeeping.

aj: agree. also we should add an invariant check in page-table mutate path: verify that pt[index].owner == expected_gpu || pt[index] == NULL before writing. will catch races earlier. but careful about perf.

maria: i'm going to run two experiments: (1) barrier-on-evict (sync DMA) on H100 to see if leak disappears, (2) invariant-assert with low-frequency sampling. will post results.

kai: sounds good. if (1) fixes it we can design a cheaper fence that only applies when chosen-kernel == concurrent-fused. also consider GC: coalesce small free fragments on long contexts to avoid fragmentation blowup.

maria: quick followup — i ran the barrier-on-evict test with 10m trial; memory stopped growing. perf hit measured ~4% P99 increase for that model.

neha: 4% P99 is acceptable for now as emergency fix. we should still dig into kernel/dma path and try to make a non-blocking fix (e.g., deferred free via freelist with confirmation token).

aj: logging task: (A) add sampled invariant checks, (B) centralize dma completion callback to single thread that enqueues free pages, (C) telemetry event for double-push. i'll file a PR.

maria: thanks — filing issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4823 (brief notes + dump). ping @kai @sanjay for review when ready. :thumbsup:

kai: thanks — please include allocation counters and kernel-selection histogram in the issue so eng-infra can correlate. :eyes:
